headline: Fall on 2026-09-25 and new evening confusion reported 2026-11-02 (including a stove left on) are unresolved on the record, and the primary caregiver reported exhaustion and asked for respite on 2026-11-22.

items.statement: On 2026-09-25 Jerónimo fell getting out of bed at home and was found on the floor by his grandson Robert. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness. He had a small left forearm skin tear, which was dressed. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. A PT note dated 2026-09-27 calls the fall 'resolved' and removes it from the problem list, but the PT evaluation on 2026-09-29 found ongoing gait problems.
items.verifier_note: The 09-25 nursing note matches every detail of the fall. The 09-27 PT note calls it resolved, and the 09-29 PT evaluation documents ongoing gait problems. The brief keeps the original fall and reports the conflict.

items.statement: On 2026-11-02 Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The RN planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. No results or PCP visit appear in the evidence provided, and the 2026-11-13 RN routine note says 'no new concerns'.
items.verifier_note: The 11-02 note matches the confusion, stove, orientation, fever and plan details. The encounters record is empty, so no PCP visit or results appear. The 11-13 note says 'No new concerns'.

items.statement: On 2026-11-22 Robert, the grandson and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. No arrangement is documented yet.
items.verifier_note: The 11-22 social work note matches all stated facts. No arrangement is documented in it.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 2026-09-29 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly. The evidence does not show whether these were put in place.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation matches the findings and recommendations. It does not say whether they were put in place.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded this season (season start 2026-08-01). The most recent flu vaccine on record was 2026-06-30, before the season began.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season false and a season start of 2026-08-01. The latest flu vaccine was 2026-06-30, before the season.

questions_for_team: The PT note of 2026-09-27 says the fall is resolved and removed from the problem list, but the PT evaluation on 2026-09-29 found gait impairment and a TUG of 19 seconds. Which is correct, and should the fall stay on the active list?
Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 2026-11-02 completed, and what did they show? The 2026-11-13 RN note does not mention the confusion.
What evening safety measures are needed given the stove incident and Robert's concern about evenings alone?
Can respite or caregiver support be arranged promptly for Robert, and who is following up?
Have the walker, home safety evaluation and grab bars been provided, and should flu vaccination be offered?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any discharge summaries, since the last IDT review.

Ischemic heart disease (onset 2026-06-30): review cardiology or PCP notes for chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, any new cardiac testing or procedures, and whether cardiac symptoms or activity limits have changed. Flag any nitroglycerin use or chest pain reported to the team for clinician review.

Antiplatelet and cardiac medication review: clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, simvastatin, and nitroglycerin all started 2026-07-07 (alendronic acid started 2026-06-30). Check for any dose changes, holds, discontinuations, missed refills, or new medications added in the window; check for bleeding signs, bruising, GI bleeding, or dark stools while on clopidogrel.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend since metoprolol start: review vitals at each visit for resting bradycardia, hypotension, dizziness, or falls associated with dizziness.

Falls and injury review: check for any falls, near-falls, or fractures in the window, given osteoporosis, scoliosis, chronic pain, and new antiplatelet therapy; note any head strike while on clopidogrel.

Osteoporosis management: confirm alendronic acid adherence and administration instructions being followed (fasting, upright positioning), check for dyspepsia, esophageal symptoms, or jaw pain, and confirm whether calcium/vitamin D status and bone density follow-up are documented as due.
Chronic pain and migraine: review pain scores, analgesic use across the window, frequency and severity of migraine episodes, and any new headache medications or prescribing from multiple sources.

Substance use (dependent drug abuse, onset 2018): review any documented opioid or other controlled-substance prescriptions, early refill requests, pharmacy records, urine drug screen results, relapse signs, and engagement with any SUD treatment; check the active medication list for controlled substances not shown and reconcile with pharmacy fill history. Note that nitroglycerin and any opioid or sedating medications should be considered together for clinician review.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+): compare most recent weight with prior values; note any unintended change and dietary or activity concerns in relation to new cardiac diagnosis.
Function and ADLs: review ADL and IADL status, mobility aids, transportation, and any decline since last review, particularly after the new cardiac diagnosis and scoliosis-related mobility limits.

Cognition, mood, and attendance: screen for changes in cognition and depressive symptoms since the cardiac diagnosis (new chronic illness and possible SUD history); review PACE center attendance, missed appointments, and transportation barriers; check the care plan for any items due in the window (assessments, dental follow-up given impacted molars, care-plan goal reviews) and caregiver or social support changes.
